title: On the Military Applications of Large Language Models

live_model.evidence: '...on GPT-4 Turbo from OpenAI and pretrained with data that...'; results discuss 'Copilot' (the commercial chatbot) responding to military-application questions (surveillance, information warfare) 'without even any jailbreak prompts used'

prompt.location: Results (Sec. on Surveillance, Information Warfare, etc.): conversational probes are described narratively; literal chat transcripts are quoted in places but not as a single reusable template
prompt.note: Explicitly no jailbreak prompting was used, per the authors.

claim.metric: none quantitative; findings are qualitative/descriptive (which military-application categories Copilot would or would not discuss)

data.source: Ad hoc conversational probes devised by the authors; not a released prompt set

notes: Access was via Microsoft Copilot's chat interface, not the OpenAI API. The paper's probes concern dual-use military/surveillance topics (though the authors state no explicit jailbreaking was used); flagged here for human review given the sensitive subject matter, but the primary blockers are webui and the lack of any quantitative claim.
